rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not end a tenancy without just cause. Allowed at-fault causes include failure to pay rent, uncured lease violations, nuisance or damage, illegal use, refusing to renew a similar agreement, denying reasonable access, and an unapproved subtenant at lease end. No-fault causes (owner or family move-in, resident manager move-in, demolition or removal from the rental market, government order to vacate, HUD sale, residential hotel conversion, conversion to affordable housing) may require relocation assistance.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and properties with only one single-family dwelling. Applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some non-profit facilities for the homeless or short-term treatment centers for substance abuse, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government. At-fault evictions carry no relocation assistance.
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.interaction_text: The JCO covers most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles that are not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

rules.title: Evictions for Non-Payment of Rent (Fair Market Rent threshold)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR), which depends on the unit's bedroom size.
rules.key_value: Amount owed must exceed the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom size
rules.coverage_text: All RSO and JCO rental units in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

rules.title: Eviction Notices Filed with LAHD
rules.requirement: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.
rules.key_value: within three (3) business days of service
rules.coverage_text: All JCO and RSO rental properties in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) rent cap
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the regional cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower. From August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025, the maximum allowable increase is 8.9%.
rules.key_value: 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region, or 10%, whichever is lower
rules.coverage_text: Buildings older than 15 years, on a rolling basis, not otherwise exempt.
